title: Async and tasks
description: Tasks, async/await, and parallel work in C#

exercises.title: thread
exercises.description: Launch go sayHello(). Print main done. Use time.Sleep to let Task run.
hints: Offload work with `Task.Run`/`Task` factories when exercises simulate background calls.
`await Task.Delay(...)` asynchronously yields better than blocking `Thread.Sleep` in modern code.
Synchronously wait only when the sandbox lacks `async Main` (`GetAwaiter().GetResult()` as last resort).

exercises.title: Channel
exercises.description: Create ch = a queue. Send "ping" to ch in Task, receive and Console.WriteLine.
hints: `System.Threading.Channels.Channel.CreateUnbounded<T>()` models async-friendly queues.
Pair `await Writer.WriteAsync` with `await Reader.ReadAsync`.
Complete writers so readers observe termination cleanly.

exercises.title: Buffered Channel
exercises.description: Create a buffered channel with capacity 2. Send 10 and 20 without blocking. Then receive and Console.WriteLine both.
hints: Bounded producers use `Channel.CreateBounded<int>(capacity)`.
`TryWrite` succeeds without blocking until capacity is saturated.
Drain asynchronously or synchronously consistent with scaffold expectations.

exercises.title: Select Statement
exercises.description: Create two channels ch1 and ch2. Send to ch1 in Task after 10ms. Use select to receive whichever comes first.
hints: Delay senders via `await Task.Delay` before publishing into the shared channel.
Consumer awaits the first incoming message asynchronously.
Keep channel lifetimes/disposals tidy to avoid dangling writers.

exercises.title: Channel Close
exercises.description: Create channel, send 1,2,3 then close. Use range to receive until closed.
hints: Producer enumerates payloads, completes the writer, then consumer uses `await foreach` on `.ReadAllAsync()`.
Ensures orderly shutdown similar to iterating until channel closure elsewhere.

exercises.title: Fan-In Pattern
exercises.description: Create two Tasks that each send a string to a shared channel. Use a third Task to fan-in (read) from the channel and Console.WriteLine received values. Close the channel when both senders are done.
hints: Coordinate parallel producers writing into a locked `List<string>` or concurrent bag.
Sort before printing when output order must normalize racing completions.
Consider `ConcurrentQueue<T>`/`lock` scopes for illustrative mutual exclusion.

exercises.title: WaitGroup
exercises.description: Use sync.WaitGroup to launch 3 Tasks that each Console.WriteLine their number, then wait for all to complete before Console.WriteLineing "done".
hints: Fan-out work with multiple `Task` instances; synchronize completion via `await Task.WhenAll`.
Alternatively sequential `.Wait()` per task when simplifying for stdout ordering.
Emit the final done line only after worker tasks finish printing.
